concept.title: Why this can be trusted
concept.shortdesc: People set the categories, every label has a quoted reason, personal details are removed, and quality is judged by whether people can find what they need.

dlentry.dd: The computer proposes groups. People decide what becomes a category and why, and each category records the user need that justifies it.

dlentry.dt: Every label has a quoted reason
dlentry.dd: No claim about who may use a service is accepted without the words from the listing that support it.
This happens before any AI model sees the text.

dlentry.dt: Bulk processing stays on the project's own computer
dlentry.dd: Listings are not sent to an outside service to be read in bulk.
It is always possible to say which version of the classification and which model produced a label.

dlentry.dt: Quality is judged by whether people can find what they need
dlentry.dd: A catalogue of real needs is the test, for example “as a carer of someone with dementia, I need a few hours' break during the day”. The bar is highest for safety-critical needs and lower for leisure.

dlentry.dt: Accuracy is measured on a hand-checked sample
dlentry.dd: The sample is labelled independently of the model that named the categories.
